items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The show had Hazel Scott, the Golden Gate Quartet, two sisters who danced East Indian dances named the Craft Sisters, Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons, the two boogie woogie pianists. With our trio of piano, bass and trumpet, we took care of the dancing.

ctx.x: This club, which was actually called Cafe Society Downtown, was at Sheridan Square and was owned by a man named Barney Josephson. The manager was Harold Johnson and a great barman called Lew. I will mention why Lew was a great barman to me later. There were four acts in the show and I know that three of them were discovered by and sponsored by John Hammond.

Boogie Woogie was popular and John had put it together the three greatest exponents of that style of piano playing. They were Meade Lux Lewis, Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons. But the Cafe only Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons were working as a team, and there was a great blues singer named "Big" Joe Turner whom the two boogie woogie pianists accompanied. And the three of them would really rock the joint every night. And they could drink plenty of booze and carry it well.

Another act was called the Golden Gate Quartet. Their names were Bill Johnson, Clyde Redick, Wilson and . They had a style of singing gospel songs which I had never heard before. In fact I didn't know anything about gospel singing except what I had heard in Baptist churches. But this was more like Holy-Holy singing to me, because it had a jazz rhythm and these fellows slap their thighs with their hands in four-four rhythm; and Yank accompanied them on drums with wire brushes on the snare drum and the joint kept…
